newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says wants to be major gas supplier to Europe.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says wants to be major gas supplier to Europe.

text.p: Iraq wants to be a major supplier of gas to countries in southern Europe after U.N. sanctions are lifted, Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said in remarks published on Tuesday.
"The (Iraqi) oil ministry is seeking...to be a major supplier of gas to southern Europe after the unjust embargo on Iraq is lifted, Rasheed told the government newspaper al-Jumhoriya.
He said Iraq was the only country which had a large number of discovered oil and gas fields waiting for development.

Rasheed put Iraq's gas reserves at 110 trillion cubic metres distributed in the south and north of the country. Official estimates put proven gas reserves at more than 3,115 billion cubic metres (10,217 billion cubic feet) in 1989.
Last May Iraq signed with Turkey a gas deal to build a 1,300 km long (800-mile) pipeline capable of carrying 10 billion cubic metres of gas from Iraqi fields to Turkish ports.

Officials of both countries said then that the pipeline would supply gas to European countries in addition to meeting Turkey's needs after the end of the U.N. sanctions, imposed on Iraq after its August 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Rasheed also said that Baghdad intended to develop its oil exports facilities in cooperation with foreign companies to enable Iraq to export six million barrels per day (bpd) after the sanctions.
Rasheed did not name these companies, however.
The U.N. has allowed Baghdad since December last year to sell a limited amount of oil worth $2 billion over six months to buy humanitarian needs of Iraqis.
Iraq has said that its pipelines and ports would be able to handle six million bpd within five years of the sanctions being lifted.
